title: Own a pharmacy business only as a pharmacist or another permitted owner
what: Only a pharmacist (or another person the Act allows) may own, or hold an interest in, a pharmacy business.

sources.title: Pharmacy Act 2010 (WA)
sources.quote: 54. Ownership of, and interests in, pharmacy business (1) A person must not own, or hold a proprietary interest in, a pharmacy business unless the person is — (a) a pharmacist; or (b) a person who is a partner in a partnership that carries on the business and in which every partner is either — (i) a pharmacist; or (ii) a close family member of a partner who is a pharmacist; or (c) a pharmacist controlled company; or (d) a friendly society; or (e) the preserved company.

confidence_note: The Act's own words reserve ownership of pharmacy businesses to pharmacists and the other owners it lists.

assessment.summary: Only pharmacists may own pharmacies, and each may own only a few. It keeps other investors and business models out of community pharmacy; the Harper Review recommended removing the restriction.

marks.reason: Reserves ownership of pharmacies to pharmacists and caps how many each may own: an exclusive right to enter.

assessment.confidence_note: The restriction is explicit; its effect on prices and access has not been measured in Australia. Marks copied from the register item wa-pharmacy-ownership so the two agree.
